name: Multi/Hyperspectral Image Compression Benchmark
description: This paper benchmarks three multi/hyperspectral image compression approaches: the classic Multi-2D compression approach and two different implementations of 3D approach (Full 3D and Hybrid). All approaches are combined with a spectral PCA decorrelation stage to optimize performance. These three compression approaches are compared within a larger comparison framework than the conventionally used PSNR, which includes eight metrics divided into three families. The comparison is carried out with regard to variations in bitrates, spatial, and spectral dimensions variations of images. The time and memory consumption difference between the three approaches is also discussed. Results of this comparison show the weaknesses and strengths of each approach.
evaluation_method: rate-distortion and fidelity metrics (PSNR, SSIM, spectral distortion measures) together with bitrate / compression ratio and runtime/memory profiling
general_score_metric: rate-distortion (PSNR vs bitrate) / spectral distortion metrics
reputation: Niche, technical benchmark used within the hyperspectral/multispectral compression research community for comparative algorithm studies.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focusing on algorithmic compression trade-offs; multiple complementary metrics (no single dominant score); results sensitive to data spectral/spatial characteristics and implementation choices; computational cost and memory use are important factors.
